name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?

- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results yet. With 2 seeds the starting architecture scored 0.000, so the first goal is any nonzero success. It already has a 1x1 column encoder, two 3x3 convolutions and per-type footprint pooling, so it may be short of samples rather than structure. At the default recipe it gets 131k steps, about 8k episodes, and the +1 exact-build bonus at episode end is discounted heavily at gamma 0.95. All 3 candidates share one recipe so that architecture comparisons are clean: 2 PPO epochs (about 243k steps), gamma 0.99, gae_lambda 0.95 and ent_coef 0.005. Candidate 1 isolates the recipe. Candidate 2 refines the architecture: LayerNorm residual blocks and learned convolutions shaped like each brick footprint. Candidate 3 tests a new idea: per-layer features with a learned soft choice of landing layer. Each design stays at or below the starting compute so it keeps the full step budget. Every file reads grid size and footprints from spec.

### Round 2
All three round-1 trials scored exactly 0 on dev and 0 in training, so the results don't tell them apart. Training runs took 73–141 s against a 900 s cap, so the compute budget limits us, not time. The three trials had very different spatial heads and all failed identically, so I have three guesses about why. (1) Too few samples: the default per-sample cost and epochs allow only about 230k steps. (2) Every head assumes action index = type·Y·X + y·X + x, matching cell (y, x) in the observation. This world 'may differ', and a transposed or permuted layout would defeat any purely local convolutional head. (3) The policy may settle early on calling DONE, which avoids the per-step and extra-cell penalties. This round tests (1) with 1 PPO epoch (about 1.85x more samples). It tests (2) by adding a cheap position-specific flat linear head that can learn any mapping from cells to actions, on two different trunks.

### Round 3
All six trials score exactly 0 on dev and 0 on training success. That includes 2-3x more samples, normalised trunks and flat position-specific heads. Getting no exact builds at all, even in training, points to a structural block rather than slow learning. The likeliest one is DONE. DONE is 1 of about 250 actions. Early on, ending gives 0 reward while placing gives dense positive reward, so the shared softmax pushes DONE toward zero. It is then almost never sampled at the moment the build is complete. Greedy evaluation keeps placing and ruins every finished build. A second possible block is that the action layout may be transposed or flipped relative to the observation. A shift-invariant conv head cannot learn that, and a flat head learns it too slowly. This round tests DONE parameterisations that do not dilute DONE, plus one candidate that also covers dihedral layouts. All use r2c1's recipe.

### Round 4
Every trial so far scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success, across 18 seeds. That covers bigger budgets (1 epoch, about 400k steps), normalised trunks, footprint-shaped heads, a flat head, reworked DONE logits and flipped or transposed heads. A per-placement reward this dense should teach a conv net to fill missing cells. If even sampled training builds never succeed, the outputs probably do not line up with the real actions. Two layouts would explain this and are not yet covered. If actions are ordered cell first and type second, every conv head is scrambled. If DONE sits at index 0, our DONE logit lands on an illegal placement, so the agent can never stop and never builds exactly. This is the last round, and any nonzero result wins. I test learned heads for each of these layouts, small at the start and added to the start network, plus one fully general head that learns which cell each action uses.
